# The IronAuth SDK contract

The wire formats an SDK may depend on, and what it may depend on them FOR.

Every value below is read out of the code that implements it, so this document
cannot describe a cookie name or an error code the server does not actually use.
The prose is hand-written; the values are not.

## Stability policy

Three tiers, because "stable" without a scope is a promise nobody can keep.

| Tier | What it covers | What we promise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Contract** | Cookie NAMES, the CSRF rule, error-code wire strings, and the management API surface published in `docs/openapi/management.json` | No breaking change without a major version and one minor release of deprecation notice. Additions are not breaking. |
| **Observable** | Cookie ATTRIBUTES (`SameSite`, `Max-Age`, `Path`), response ordering, and error `description` text | May change in any release. Depend on the presence of a cookie, never on its attributes; branch on the error CODE, never on its description. |
| **Internal** | Cookie VALUES and their crypto envelope, session storage, and anything under a path not in the published spec | No promises at all. A value that decodes today may not tomorrow, by design. |

The split is deliberate. An SDK that reads a cookie's *value* has coupled itself to
a sealing format that exists to be changed when the threat model changes, and
freezing it would mean choosing SDK convenience over the ability to rotate a
construction. Reading its *presence* costs nothing and never breaks.

## Cookies

| Name | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `__Host-ironauth_session` | The OP session. An SDK reads its presence, never its contents: the value is opaque and its envelope is not contract. |
| `__ironauth_opbs` | OP browser state for session management (OIDC Session Management 1.0). Not `__Host-` prefixed because the session-management iframe must read it from a sibling origin. |
| `__Host-ironauth_magic_binding` | Binds a magic-link click to the browser that requested it, so a forwarded link cannot complete in another browser. |
| `__Host-ironauth_trusted_device` | Marks a device the user has previously vouched for, so a step-up can be skipped where policy allows. |

The `__Host-` prefix is not decoration. It is enforced by the browser: a
`__Host-` cookie must be `Secure`, must have `Path=/`, and must carry NO `Domain`
attribute, which makes it unsettable by a sibling subdomain. An SDK that sees the
prefix can rely on that without asking the server.

## CSRF

State-changing interaction endpoints require a same-origin request, decided from
the browser-set `Sec-Fetch-Site` fetch-metadata header rather than from a token an
SDK would have to fetch and echo.

There is no CSRF token to read, mint, or forward. A cross-site value is refused;
a same-origin value and an absent header are allowed, because a header the browser
did not set is not evidence of anything and older browsers omit it. An SDK driving
these endpoints from a browser needs to do nothing; one driving them from a server
is not making a cross-site request in the first place.

## Error codes

The authorization endpoint's machine-readable codes. 10 of them, taken
from the exhaustive match that renders them, so this list cannot fall behind the
code without the freshness gate failing.

| Code | Rust variant |
| --- | --- |
| `access_denied` | `AuthzErrorCode::AccessDenied` |
| `account_selection_required` | `AuthzErrorCode::AccountSelectionRequired` |
| `consent_required` | `AuthzErrorCode::ConsentRequired` |
| `interaction_required` | `AuthzErrorCode::InteractionRequired` |
| `invalid_request` | `AuthzErrorCode::InvalidRequest` |
| `invalid_target` | `AuthzErrorCode::InvalidTarget` |
| `login_required` | `AuthzErrorCode::LoginRequired` |
| `server_error` | `AuthzErrorCode::ServerError` |
| `unmet_authentication_requirements` | `AuthzErrorCode::UnmetAuthenticationRequirements` |
| `unsupported_response_type` | `AuthzErrorCode::UnsupportedResponseType` |

**Branch on the code, never on the description.** The `description` is prose for a
human reading a log; it is Observable tier and will change. The code is Contract.

Several of these are deliberately indistinguishable from one another on the wire in
cases where telling them apart would answer a question the caller has not earned:
an unknown client and a client presented under the wrong scope are one response, so
the endpoint is not an oracle for which tenants exist.
